newsitem.title: USA: Ruling expected Friday in Simpson custody battle.
newsitem.headline: Ruling expected Friday in Simpson custody battle.

text.p: A judge was expected to issue a ruling on Friday in O.J. Simpson's battle for custody of the two children he had with Nicole Brown Simpson, a court clerk said.
Judge Nancy Wieben Stock, the Orange County family court judge presiding over the custody case, planned to release her written decision on Friday after 4:15 p.m. PST (7:15 p.m. EST), the clerk said.

Louis and Juditha Brown, who have been taking care of 11- year-old Sydney and 8-year-old Justin since shortly after their mother's 1994 murder, had been notified that a ruling was imminent, but there was no word of what the judge had decided.

Simpson, a former football star with a more recent career in movies and television ads, was acquitted in October 1995 in the killings of his ex-wife and her friend Ronald Goldman. Simpson is on trial in civil court facing a wrongful death lawsuit brought by the victims' families.
Simpson turned over temporary guardianship of the children to their maternal grandparents after his June 17, 1994, arrest, but now he wants them back.
Closing arguments in the closed-door custody case ended on December 11 in Orange County family court. The judge took the matter "under submission" and said she would issue a written decision later.
Attorneys for Louis and Juditha Brown, the children's maternal grandparents, contended Simpson was an unfit parent, citing allegations that he beat and threatened his ex-wife.

But Simpson's lawyers argued he had a right to full custody as the biological father. Simpson reportedly also expressed concern that living with the Browns, who are white, his children were not being properly instructed in their black heritage.
